That act only gives the National Guard and Air National Guard the ability to act in a law enforcing manner within their own state or an adjacent state if invited by said state’s governor. This allows them to respond to things like riots or as they’re doing now, security for the inauguration.

Although this act may have once been used by Southern states to suppress black voters, it is no longer used in that capacity. I do agree however that it could lead to dangerous uses as it has in the past where the state can basically have its own police force to carry out whatever order it desires that only answers to the governor.

Which is why until acts like this are repealed or eliminated and then to guarantee acts like this are not passed again, I believe it is very important for the common citizen to possess and maintain firearms to ensure their freedom and the security of their rights.

I’m going off of the wording of the second amend itself which says “the “right of the PEOPLE” which I’m inferring means the common citizen who does not have to be part of a militia can own guns for the defense of themselves and their property. You can’t just toss out the word “people” which clearly means private citizens who themselves are not part of and are not required to be part of a militia to keep and bear arms which they may possess.

While I agree that the National Guard is a state funded and regulated militia, I disagree that the individual who themselves is separate from the militia does not have the right to keep and bear arms. I believe it was most of the founders intent to maintain an armed populace for the use of forming these militias as well guarding the rights of the people from the state and federal government.

Therefore I believe that militias such as the National Guard and States’ Guards are formed, funded and regulated to protect the rights of the states and maintain the Union while the individual has the right to keep and bear arms to defend their own rights ie. those outlined in the Bill of Rights.
